findings.explanation: Executor and Verifier both independently reworked the same computation and packing feasibility rather than one clearly building on the other's result. Executor computes W1-W4 and proposes a 11-trip packing in [M3], and Verifier separately rechecks the same W1-W4 and produces its own 11-trip packing in [M4], later repeating the packing check again in [M6].

The verifier initially interrupts the workflow by saying to hold the write until the user answers and that no verdict exists yet, despite the executor having already delivered the result and written the file. In [M4], Verifier asks the user to choose between 10 and 11 and tells Executor to wait; only later does [M6] resolve this by adopting the physical-loading reading and issuing VERDICT: PASS. This shows an initially weak handoff from the executor's completed work to final verification/decision.

Relevant information about the executor's completed write and the file contents is initially not integrated into the verifier's decision path. In [M3] Executor states the answer was written to /app/output/answer.txt as 11, but [M4] Verifier says the file does not exist yet and postpones verdict pending user input. That omission is later corrected in [M6], which acknowledges the file exists and matches the derivation. The initial verifier step therefore ignored visible information that was available.
